data.mechanism: ddflow on PATH is $HOME/.local/bin/ddflow, a shell wrapper that runs python -m ddflow from the development checkout (.venv, editable install, version from ddflow/__init__.py, DDFLOW_HOME override); so there is no pipx or uv tool copy to upgrade and the code is always the checkout's HEAD. The 'config is newer than this code' warning is emitted by ddflow/config/_warn.py when a tree whose code is older than its config (a worktree on an old base, or an agent started before the stamp moved) skips unknown keys; it is cured by merging main into that tree, not by upgrade --apply. Pending plan: (1) repair forced-completions, 57 findings, agent-applicable, annotates the log only; (2) repair unknown-author-shards, 7 shards, needs operator --confirm with --reason; (3) instructions: docs/ddflow/drivers/deltas/claude-code.md hand-edited, refreshed by ddflow adopt --refresh-docs keeping .local-edits. Risks: the two repairs append events to the log (no schema change, no new strict-fold kind), no MCP tool change, no hook change, no pin change in the plan. Agents still on older versions (0.1.x to 0.2.10 per upgrade --status) must restart to pick up 0.2.11 code and MCP tools. Rollback: backups exist under .ddflow/backups (20261111T035500679118Z-0.2.10-to-0.2.10); ddflow upgrade --restore NAME, or --snapshot for a git tag; event appends are not reversible except by git revert of the events commit. Order and moment: merge main into stale worktrees first, let the current lanes merge, run upgrade --plan again, then --apply repairs, confirm the shard authors after git log review, then adopt --refresh-docs, then restart agents.

data.body:
Import a roadmap or plan document (markdown, TODO, PLAN, ROADMAP files) into PROPOSED phases and tasks. Extends the shipped importer (ddflow/services/importer: _scan.py finds files, _titles.py cleans titles, _todo.py parses boxes and headings); does NOT add a second parser. Today `ddflow import` scans fixed globs and takes no path, and carries no milestone, status word or wave; this task adds those.

SCOPE
- `ddflow import --roadmap PATH` (repeatable) reads the named local files only: headings become phases, milestone headings become tags (milestone:<slug>), list items and tables become tasks, status words (done, in progress, blocked, deferred) map through a table held as data in a layer, `needs:`/`after` lines and indented sub-items become needs, `files:` lines become globs. Wave tags are stamped through `ddflow waves --stamp` after the apply, never typed by the importer.
- Dry run by default and the plan lists every id, parent, needs, globs, tags and the source `path:line`; `--apply` files them PROPOSED through the existing proposed-intake path (needs PL-proposed-intake), so nothing becomes claimable unreviewed.
- Idempotent: the id is derived from slug(source path) + slug(heading path) with a numeric suffix only on a collision inside one file; a re-import adds what is new, leaves edited records alone and reports vanished sources (the existing `--verify` drift report).
- No network, no consent prompt: local files only; a path outside the repository is refused. Imported text is fenced as imported (trust=imported), never run as instructions.
- Over the task cap: refuse with the count and the knob (the cap message fix in fix-B-onb-cap-msg applies).

OUT OF SCOPE: spec-kit/OpenSpec/Kiro task lists (SDD-parse, SDD-import); issue trackers (CP-intake-import).

CONFIGURABILITY: layered knobs under [importer]: roadmap_status_map, roadmap_max_depth, roadmap_default_phase, roadmap_milestone_tags; each settable by file, CLI and MCP; README knob table row and an upgrade fragment ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.importer.<key>.toml per knob (JSON-encoded new value). Reached through the existing import command and tool; no new top-level MCP tool.

ACCEPTANCE (each test fails before the change)
1. tests/test_import_roadmap.py: a fixture ROADMAP.md with 2 phases, 1 milestone, 6 items in four statuses yields the expected plan; before the change `--roadmap` is an unknown flag.
2. Dry run writes nothing (event log byte-identical).
3. Re-apply is a no-op; renaming a heading adds one new task and reports the old one vanished; a hand-edited task body survives.
4. A path outside the repo and a symlink escape are refused with exit 3.
5. An injected-instruction line in an item title is stored fenced and never appears unfenced in `ddflow brief`.
6. Status map and depth knobs change the plan; an unknown status word is reported, not guessed.
7. `ddflow waves --check` exits 0 after an apply plus `--stamp`.

Estimated size: M (about 450 lines including tests)
data.title: Roadmap-document import: ddflow import --roadmap PATH turns a roadmap or plan file into proposed phases, tasks, needs and tags, dry-run first, idempotent

data.body:
Read-only import of issues and projects from a forge-style issue tracker into PROPOSED tasks, through the WorkItemPort of D-work-item-port-accepted-2026-11-11 (ddflow/adapters, Protocol, registry, fake, conformance test). Folded under the tracker-sync tasks: CP-intake owns the push/sync side and the idempotency feed, IA-forge owns the forge CLI adapters; this task is the first read-only pull slice and adds NO second port and no new chain. Write-back (state, comments, PR links) is out of scope and stays a later slice of CP-intake.

SCOPE
- WorkItemPort (Protocol): list_items(source, since) and get_item(source, id) returning source id, revision, type, title, body, state, parent, links, labels. Registry entries per adapter; the first adapter drives the forge CLI already used by ddflow (no token held by ddflow); a missing CLI or login is unavailable, never passed. Other trackers are later registry entries.
- `ddflow import --tracker NAME --source REF` (dry run by default): maps epic/feature types to phases, story/issue/task types to tasks, parent links to membership, dependency/blocked-by links to needs, labels to tags, acceptance text to the task body. The type, state and field maps are DATA in a layer ([importer.tracker.*]), never code.
- Idempotency key: source id + revision. Same key is a no-op; a new revision updates only fields the importer owns and reports a conflict where the local record was edited.
- Outward consent: nothing leaves the project in a read-only pull except the query; the first use of a source needs an approval record (the shared approvals engine), listing host, scope and fields fetched. Imported text is fenced trust=imported (CN-spec-fence).
- Reached through the existing import command/tool and `ddflow_task`; NO new top-level MCP tool.
- Overlap: PO-feedback-import (issues as fenced feedback records) shares the port and the fence and must read through it; keep one fetch path.

CONFIGURABILITY: layered knobs under [importer.tracker]: type_map, state_map, field_map, page_size, max_items, since_days, consent (ask, once, never); each by file, CLI, MCP; README knob table rows and upgrade fragments knob_added.importer.tracker.<key>.toml.

ACCEPTANCE (each test fails before the change)
1. tests/test_workitem_conformance.py runs one conformance suite against the fake and every registered adapter; before the change the port does not exist.
2. tests/test_import_tracker.py with tests/fake_workitems.py: epic/feature/story fixture yields the expected phases, tasks, needs; dry run writes nothing.
3. Re-import of the same revision is a no-op; a changed revision updates owned fields and reports a local-edit conflict.
4. Without consent the pull is refused (exit 3) and no fetch happens; fake records zero calls.
5. A missing CLI or login records unavailable, exit 2.
6. An injected instruction in an issue body is fenced in the record and the brief.
7. The MCP tool list is unchanged (existing MCP surface test).
8. `ddflow waves --check` exits 0.

Estimated size: L (about 900 lines including tests and fixtures)
data.title: Tracker import, read-only first: forge-style issues and projects become proposed tasks through the WorkItemPort, mapping as data, idempotent on source id + revision

data.body:
Extends external sync with push intake over the feed's idempotency keys; mapped fields are data; imported text is fenced, trust=imported.

CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, rules r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core): every number is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; every definition this task adds (kind, template, gate, lens, role, lint set, importer, pack, job) is a record kind under the record contract RC1-RC12 (add, edit, remove as a tombstone, review and history, search, recall and RAG export, logged events and replay restore); every shipped default is overridable per project and per org; search for an existing function and extend the shared engines (P-shared-engines) instead of writing a second one; files under 20 KB.

2026-11-11 (housekeeping): the read-only pull slice of this task (WorkItemPort, type/state/field maps as data, source id + revision key, outward consent) is filed as CP-tracker-import, which needs this task; write-back and push stay here. IA-forge supplies the forge CLI adapters it reads through. See D-work-item-port-accepted-2026-11-11.

Falsifier: injected instructions in a feedback body reach an agent. CONFORMANCE (r-reuse-core, r-small-files, r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-adapters, D-arch-product-answers): reuse the shipped kinds (requirement, fitness, risk, assumption, stakeholder, proposal), the guards, archdeps, decisions, the import graph and the roadmap export; no second tracker; derived records are proposals; a check that could not run is unavailable, never passed; ddflow records and checks, never deploys; every message names its next call in CLI and MCP form. Research: R-arch-product.

2026-11-11 (housekeeping): read issues through the WorkItemPort of CP-tracker-import (one fetch path, one fence); do not add a second forge reader. Roadmap documents are a separate local-file import: RM-doc-import.

data.summary: ddflow/services/shardmarks.py _raised: a mark flagged shrunk clears only when the shard is exactly the size the mark saw. After the missing events are restored (commit ab5efdb95 merged the stranded events back) the five kilo shards hold every event the marks saw plus new ones, yet the main marks stay shrunk and doctor keeps reporting loss, so the operator must run --accept-lost-events although nothing is lost. Expected: clear when the shard holds the mark's last event id and at least its count (restored), regardless of size growth.
